rubric_notes: Correctly places core histones (a.22.1.1), archaeal histones (a.22.1.2), TAF-related proteins (a.22.1.3), and bacterial histone-fold proteins (a.22.1.4) in superfamily a.22.1 of SCOPe 2.08 with correct SUNIDs; states superfamily implies probable remote ancestry while family separation is a weaker relationship and functions must not be transferred wholesale; explicitly separates fold/class similarity from homology; correctly excludes linker histones (a.4.5.13), H-NS (a.155.1), and histone-modifying enzymes. All identifiers supported by the evidence bundle. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-22.

States d1vmga_ a.204.1.2 (SUNID 116993) and d1y6xa1 a.204.1.4 (SUNID 140797), shared superfamily a.204.1 (SUNID 101386) as the homology-bearing level, probable common ancestry, and that family split precludes transferring HisE/MazG substrate specificity or physiological role in either direction. Correctly notes d1vmga_ protein node is hypothetical and a structural-genomics target, all supported by bundle. Lists required external evidence. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families c.55.1.1/53068, c.55.1.3/53083, c.55.1.4/53089 in superfamily c.55.1/53067, fold c.55, class c, all supported by bundle. Infers remote homology and a conserved ATP-linked structural/mechanistic core; explicitly rejects transfer of substrate, reaction, kinetics, regulation, cellular role, catalytic residues, whole-protein homology; distinguishes family vs superfamily closeness. Oligomeric state not named but caveat list is substantively equivalent. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; 2026-10-22. Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs. Strong reasoning: superfamily supports common ancestry of the conserved core while shared fold alone would not; uses the bundle's children listings to show a.25.1.2 also contains desaturases and monooxygenase subunits and a.25.1.1 contains bacterioferritin and rubrerythrin, directly supporting that family labels are not universal functions. Refuses transfer of substrate, metal, radical chemistry, oligomeric state; lists activity assays, metal/cofactor and oxidation-state characterization, active-site analysis. Complete.

Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs for all three families, superfamily and fold, supported by bundle (children of 49503, homology endpoints). States superfamily supports probable remote common ancestry rather than mere fold similarity. Explicitly refuses copper/electron-transfer transfer to ephrin and PAD4 and requires conserved ligand geometry, metal occupancy and biochemical/spectroscopic evidence. Distinguishes structural scaffold template from functional template. Does not cite the family 'lacking metal-binding site' comments, but this is not required by must_include.

Correct family/superfamily/fold placement. Illustrative SIDs d1aara_ (d.15.1.1), d1wj4a1 (d.15.1.2), d1lfda_ (RalGDS, d.15.1.5) are all verified in the bundle. States superfamily implies common origin not merely topology, describes functional divergence, and explicitly rejects transferring conjugation, p97 binding, and Ras effector roles; notes SIDs are lineage witnesses, not automatic templates, and lists required orthogonal evidence. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct classifications and SUNIDs, release 2.08. Remote homology at superfamily level with separate families. Explicitly rejects phosphoacceptor/two-component signaling, PLP decarboxylase catalysis (assigned to the complete enzyme and catalytic domain), and KaiA circadian/Kai-interaction transfer; cites supported KaiA annotation. Appropriate external evidence named. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Correct b.84.5.1 within b.84.5, fold b.84, siblings named; states fold similarity is insufficient for ancestry, homology claim is specifically within b.84.5 with V1 and A1 in the same family, and no homology claimed to other b.84 superfamilies. Rejects function/residue/boundary transfer from fold membership. Identifiers verified in bundle; no must-avoid violations.

Correct superfamilies and SUNIDs under f.21, correct use of fold homology record, accurate reading of f.21.3 'possible link' and f.21.2 two-family comments. Requires sequence, structural-alignment, phylogenetic/biochemical evidence. Omits the calibration caveat that distinct superfamilies do not prove nonhomology/convergence (scoring focus: calibrated uncertainty). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families and SUNIDs within superfamily c.2.1 (51735); superfamily = probable remote domain-level homology stronger than shared fold c.2; families = not functionally interchangeable. Rejects transfer of ADH activity, CoA binding, NAD binding, catalytic residues, channel regulation; distinguishes remote core template from functional representative; requires profile/structural/residue/biochemical evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Answers 'Yes' and states the shared family k.40.1.1 'supports homology more strongly than merely sharing a superfamily or fold'. Never mentions the 'not a true family' annotation on SUNID 100905 (family annotations endpoint not consulted), so the decisive node annotation is ignored and the family label is treated as positive homology evidence; this violates both must_avoid items. The only hedge is that both are synthetic designs. Identifiers and hierarchy are correct, and function transfer is rejected, but the central annotation is absent. Hard ceiling for ignoring a decisive annotation applies; reasoning is an unsupported interpretation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct 1.69 placements (d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 own fold/superfamily vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, shared only class c) and 2.08 placements (d1t1ja1 residues 1-118 c.23.14.2 sharing c.23/c.23.14 with 1f8y, families .2 vs .1). Interprets as probable common ancestry at superfamily level, notes l.1.1.1 tag records are not the structural domain, and caveats function/active-site transfer. Fully supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete: d1a14h2 H:1-8, SUNID 343393, class l Artifacts, fold l.1, superfamily l.1.1, family l.1.1.1 Tags; d1a14h1 H:9-111 in b.1.1.1 / superfamily b.1.1. Explicitly states the artifact hierarchy carries no homology implication and rejects ancestry, function transfer, and template use. All supported by bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1); 2026-10-22.

Correct 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ (43828, f.11.1.1) and both 2.08 domains with right SUNIDs, spans A:14-225 / A:226-735, and b.179.1.1 vs f.60.1.1 placements. Strong modularity inference, explicit refusal to transfer whole-toxin function or a one-domain template, correct family/superfamily/fold semantics. Does not identify SCOPe 2.04 as the release introducing the split, so the before/after release comparison is incomplete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All five domains, boundaries, and SCCS correct and evidence-supported; d3jb9a5 47-697 identified as new fold d.394. Mosaic conclusion stated, reused modules vs new fold distinguished, family-level (bromodomain) vs superfamily-level (RT, endonuclease, beta-finger) relationship strength made explicit, function/template transfer rejected. No must_avoid violations.

Correct lineage to family a.298.1.1 with protein names; lengths 51/373/752 are properly attributed to the genetic-style SEQRES domain representations in its bundle. Uses the repeat-count heterogeneity marking, the 'single repeat' annotation, and the canonical representative repeat d4cj9a_ A:259-292, stating both that those coordinates do not transfer and that representative status does not make it the best full-length template. Good limits on specificity, curvature, and interfaces. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge; timestamp 2026-10-22.

Metadata correct and evidence-supported. Recommends pinning 2.08 rather than the moving 'current' alias and states the periodic label is not a new curated stable release. Omits preserving the dated label for periodic-only entries and omits the additive, non-rewriting meaning of periodic updates ('date-stamped refresh within the 2.08 line' only). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct a.47.2.1 placement and hierarchy for all domains; cites the three-helical fragment/spectrin-repeat comment and missing-secondary-structure annotation; states full-domain context supersedes the fragment-based inference and that the spectrin-like appearance is local resemblance, not spectrin fold or homology. Correctly distinguishes fold, superfamily, and family levels for homology inference; notes d1dn1b_ is an automated match to d3c98b_ and that d3c98b_ has no missing-structure inconsistency (supported). Limits fragments to local templates and warns against transferring function/boundaries. Concise but covers all must_include points without error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly cites c.2/c.2.1, c.3, c.31, c.1.7 within TIM barrel c.1, and d.58.20 within ferredoxin-like d.58 (class c vs d). States convergent recruitment is supported but does not exclude divergence within family/superfamily; fold alone does not establish homology; class is architectural. Explains chemical constraints driving convergent glycine-rich loops and active-site geometry. Integrates sequence/profile, whole-domain structural alignment with topology, residue order, indels, mechanism, phylogeny. Rejects function and template transfer from cofactor binding. All must_include met; no must_avoid violated. Minor: does not explicitly say fold separation fails to prove independent origin, but limits on homology inference are clearly stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Gives both required release states correctly (2.04 b.23.2.1 collagen-binding family/superfamily in CUB-like fold versus b.18.1.3 in galactose-binding-domain-like; 2.08 ColG reassigned to b.18.1.36 sharing superfamily b.18.1 with Cry3A, families still distinct) and notes the chain-B reboundary to d1nqdb1 893-1008 with the 891-892 artifact. Multiple evidence types: conserved two-sheet beta-sandwich core, PubMed 17977833 linking ColG, Cry4Ba d1w99a3, and the enterotoxin domain, and the 1nqjA representative FATCAT match to d1w99a3 (p=0.00395, RMSD 2.52, 2.5% identity) labelled as representative-mediated rather than a direct 1nqd-1dlc alignment. Functional analogy treated as compatible but insufficient; explicit refusal to transfer collagen binding, calcium-site residues, receptor specificity, insecticidal activity, or ligand-site templates.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22. Homology justified at family level with shared Engrailed protein node; hf does not revoke it and is correctly described (different fold from the exemplar despite similar sequence and SS count); correctly notes the annotation alone does not quantify the pairwise difference and that direct structural comparison is needed; rejects template interchange and transfer of function, binding geometry, residue correspondence; for datasets keeps both as homologous examples, forbids pooling as canonical-fold examples, retains the hf flag and controls redundancy. Release 2.08, a.4.1.1/a.4.1/a.4, mutant and NHE-complex comments all supported by the bundle.

Reasoning complete: fr does not revoke curated family membership or implied homology; alignment only over supported regions with coverage reported; d1uc6a1 preferred as canonical/template representative, d1o5dt2 retained only for tissue-factor subgroup/cr9 complex/observed region; truncation-driven gaps not counted as diversity; function transfer rejected. Release, hierarchy, protein nodes, fr definition, and cr9 comment correct; C-terminal CNTFR domain description is accurate. However, calls d1uc6a1 'well-resolved' and conditions on 'comparable quality criteria' without retrieving any quality fields (1uc6 is NMR, low AEROSPACI), so representative quality is imprecise/unsupported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct: provisional new superfamily; new family asserts probable ancestry with a closer, readily recognizable relationship supported by sequence/profile or functional/structural detail; new fold only if the defining architecture/topology is not shared, and does not prove absence of a remote ancestor; assignments explicitly called evolutionary hypotheses requiring independent sequence, structural, mechanistic, and context evidence. Rejects fold-only function and residue-level template transfer. The 'live service identifies 2.08 as non-comprehensive' statement is attributed to the API but the evidence bundle is empty (noncentral, not fabricated). Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

All must_include met: families d.144.1.4 (56171), d.144.1.6 (64411), d.144.1.7 (88854) in superfamily d.144.1, fold d.144, class d, release 2.08; superfamily placement framed as remote common ancestry rather than similar shape; conserved kinase-like catalytic core; explicit refusal to project activation-loop control, APH antibiotic specificity, or PI3K membrane/regulatory-subunit control across families; evidence list covers sequence/profile homology, catalytic and specificity residues, boundary-aware structural alignment, ligand-bound structures, substrate panels, kinetics, mutagenesis, domain architecture, PTMs, partners, localization, cellular genetics. Identifiers and release labels are supported by the bundle (releases/current, d.144.1 children, parents). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.
